articles.title: Laura Fuertes peleará por el oro europeo en Sofía
articles.standfirst: Tras imponerse en semifinales a la alemana Maxi Klozer
articles.summary: Tras imponerse en semifinales a la alemana Maxi Klozer
articles.body: Laura Fuertes, que un día antes hizo historia al asegurar la primera medalla española de una boxeadora en un Europeo, ha dado un paso más este miércoles. La asturiana ha sellado el billete para la final continental de menos de 51 kilos tras imponerse en las semifinales a la alemana Maxi Klozer por decisión dividida (3-2). La gijonesa fue superior a la germana y supo mantener el control y la iniciativa a lo largo de todo el combate. Su forma de manejar la distancia, unida a su ventaja de altura y envergadura, resultaron determinantes para llevarse la victoria. Será el tercer podio de 2026 tras la lesión. Primero fue en un codo, y después la fractura en la falange del meñique derecho por la que tuvo que ser operada hace nueve meses. Ya en junio, se colgó el bronce en la Copa del Mundo de Guiyang (China). Entonces reconocía que había sido un "proceso raro y largo". Desde la operación no encontraba volver a ser yo encima del ring y volver a encontrar mis ritmos y mi boxeo. Me llené la cabeza con mil dudas y mil suposiciones, pero al fin y al cabo todo es cuestión de tiempo. Después de mucho trabajo (mental y físico) me he vuelto a encontrar", dijo. Este verano ya subió a lo más alto del podio en los Juegos Mediterráneos de Taranto en los que se impuso a la argelina Fatiha Mansouri (4-1). Fuertes derribó la primera barrera para del boxeo femenino español en 2022, convirtiéndose en la primera en ganar una medalla en un Mundial. También fue la primera boxeadora nacional en clasificarse para unos Juegos Olímpicos. Ella compitió en los de París 2024, en los que cayó en primera ronda, pero abrió una puerta que espera que otras muchas mujeres atraviesen después de ella.

articles.title: Darren Till and Mike Perry finally look to settle decade-long UFC rivalry in February 2027
articles.summary: Darren Till and Mike Perry could finally settle their long-running rivalry in 2027. The former UFC stars have been linked with a fight for almost a decade.
articles.body: Darren Till and Mike Perry could finally settle their long-running rivalry in 2027. The former UFC stars have been linked with a fight for almost a decade. Their rivalry began after Till’s breakout win over Donald Cerrone at UFC Gdansk in October 2017. However, the bout never happened in the UFC.Now, the move to the Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship has brought the matchup back into focus. BKFC founder Dave Feldman has revealed that a Till-Perry fight could take place as early as February.Darren Till vs Mike Perry could finally happen in BKFCDarren Till joined Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship in April after signing a multi-fight deal with the promotion. Mike Perry has been competing in BKFC for the past four years. That has created a new opportunity for the two longtime rivals to finally share a fight.Dave Feldman confirmed that BKFC has already tried to make the fight happen. However, Perry currently has another plan in mind.When discussing Till’s return at BKFC 94 in Manchester, Feldman told SunSport, “We tried to make [the] Mike Perry [fight] happen. But then, you know, he’s trying to do something else right now. But I think that [fight] might happen in February. But Mike, he’s trying to do something else right now.”The February target could depend on Perry’s recovery. The 35-year-old suffered a shoulder dislocation during his most recent outing late last month. He could face at least four months on the sidelines because of the injury.That timeline could still allow Perry to return for a February fight. A potential training camp would also give him time to prepare for a clash with Till.Before that matchup can be made, Till has another major challenge ahead of him. The 33-year-old is set to headline BKFC 94 against former UFC middleweight Yoel Romero.The fight has attracted plenty of attention because of the age difference between the two men. Romero is 49, making him 16 years older than Till.Feldman also revealed that Romero was the one who asked for the fight.He said, “He [Yoel] asked for it, actually. He said, ‘I want the Darren Till fight.’ And then I went back to Darren Till and I said, [Are] you interested in Yoel?’ And he’s like, ‘Yeah, but I don’t know, he’s a little old. ‘Does it really do anything for me? And I said, ‘I think it does a lot for you.’ And then he’s like, ‘Yeah, let’s have it.’ ‘Let’s absolutely have it because people think I’m afraid of him, and I’m not. And let me show the world that I’m not.’”Till will now focus on Romero before potentially turning his attention back to Perry. A February meeting would finally give the pair a chance to settle a rivalry that began in 2017.The two fighters have taken very different paths since their first confrontation. Till became a UFC title challenger, while Perry established himself as one of BKFC’s biggest names. articles.title: UFC news: Gable Steveson breaks silence on 12-second knockout loss
articles.summary: On Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026, former Olympian and WWE star Gable Steveson faced off against Sean Sharaf at UFC 331. However, their match finished even before...
articles.body:
On Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026, former Olympian and WWE star Gable Steveson faced off against Sean Sharaf at UFC 331 . However, their match finished even before it properly started. Competing in his second-ever UFC fight, Steveson suffered a humiliating knockout loss against Sharaf.

Sharaf knocked out Steveson just 12 seconds into the first round. It marked Steveson's first loss in professional MMA , taking his win-loss record to 4-1. Before this loss, Steveson had won his first three fights against Braden Peterson, Kevin Hein, Hugo Lezama, and Elisha Ellison.

Following the loss, Steveson became a topic of conversation on the internet and a victim of severe social media backlash and trolling. Now, days after his loss, Steveson has broken his silence .

"This statement is for my family, my friends, my fans, and the people who truly know me and know the kind of man I am. I know there are people who will never support me, no matter what I say or do. That's their choice. But I'm speaking to the people who know me, not just as an athlete, but as a husband and a father to a young daughter," he shared.

Steveson also addressed the sexual assault allegations from a 2019 incident in his college years that resurfaced ahead of the fight. He claimed that it was raised to get into his head. He made it clear that he did not do any of the alleged things and was never charged with a crime as well.

"The allegations were not ignored nor brushed aside. They were thoroughly and heavily reviewed as I fully cooperated with law enforcement, including a separate Title IX review. There were no criminal charges, no conviction, and no finding of responsibility against me. The matter was closed, and there is no pending legal issue involving me. My own attorney did their own investigation and stated on the record that even if the law was changed, I would have the same outcome, which now speaks for itself," he added.

He also commented on how serioes allegations like these are. However, moving forward, he wants to stay focused on his wife, daughter, and his family. "To the people who support me, thank you. I know who I am. My family knows who I am. The people who have walked with me through life know who I am. That's what matters to me, and that's where I'm going to keep my focus.

"As for my opponent, congratulations. You caught me. A mistake on my end was made. It was your night. Just like my wrestling days after my loss, I came back with an undeniable will to win and focus that led me to the top of my sport. The result of Saturday night, I believe, will catapult me to do the same. I will be great, and this won't deny me," Steveson finished.

Steveson is a 2020 U.S. Olympic wrestling gold medalist and two-time NCAA Division I national champion, a former WWE Superstar , and a member of the NFL's Buffalo Bills.
